extracted.intended_audience: screenwriters and fiction writers learning story structure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for structuring a screenplay or English-language fiction into Syd Field's three acts, with recommended page/percentage targets, key beats (inciting incident, plot points, midpoint), and quality criteria for escalation and payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act proportions (25/50/25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-act structure divides a story into Act 1 (~25%), Act 2 (~50%), and Act 3 (~25%), with specific beats approximately at 12%, 25%, 50%, and 75% of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field's 'paradigm' gives explicit page targets per act; use the percentage targets to place the inciting incident (~12%), Plot Point 1 (~25%), Midpoint (~50%), and Plot Point 2 (~75%). These proportions guide pacing and escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 1 — Setup / Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce protagonist, world, and status quo; establish stakes and tone for the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains the inciting incident (~12%) which disrupts equilibrium and Plot Point 1 (~25%) where the protagonist commits to a new course. Act 1 'promises' what the story will deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting Incident
rubrics_metrics.description: The catalyst that disrupts the equilibrium of the protagonist's world, occurring around 12% into the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should raise the central question or problem that drives the narrative; the climax must later answer this question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Point 1
rubrics_metrics.description: The approximately 25% mark where the protagonist commits to a new course of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be a consequential turning point (a 'real reversal'), not merely an event; it propels the story into Act 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 2 — Confrontation / Rising Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The middle act (~50%) in which the protagonist tries to resolve the problem and situations worsen; the longest act where escalation occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act 2 must keep escalating and is 'the hardest' to sustain. It contains the Midpoint and Plot Point 2 and should maintain internal structure (beginning/middle/end) as a fractal of the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: A major reversal or commitment around the 50% mark that shifts the story's direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The midpoint is 'load-bearing' — often a false victory or false defeat that changes stakes and intensifies escalation. It should significantly alter the protagonist's circumstances or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Point 2
rubrics_metrics.description: A setback near the 75% mark that demands a new plan from the protagonist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must function as a genuine reversal that propels the story into Act 3 and sets up the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 3 — Resolution / Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The final act (~25%) containing the climax (decisive confrontation), falling action, and the new equilibrium or resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The climax must answer the question raised by the inciting incident. Act 3 'pays off' the promises made in Act 1 and resolves the central dramatic problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractal structure (each act has beginning/middle/end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each act should contain its own beginning, middle, and end, mirroring the overall three-act structure on a smaller scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'fractal' requirement supports pacing and maintains momentum within each act; treat acts as mini-acts to preserve rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot points as real reversals
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot points must be real reversals, not just events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid superficial beats that do not change direction or stakes; each plot point should materially alter the protagonist's trajectory or the story's stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise and payoff
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setups and promises established early must be resolved and paid off by the resolution; ensure that initial promises are fulfilled by the climax and denouement.
